citation: Solow, R. 'A Contribution to the Theory of Economic Growth.' QJE 70(1)
key_claim_paraphrased: Long-run per-capita growth comes from technology; capital accumulation alone runs into diminishing returns.
lac_relevance: Baseline: LAC accumulated factors but TFP did not converge.

citation: Lewis, W.A. 'Economic Development with Unlimited Supplies of Labour.' Manchester School 22(2)
key_claim_paraphrased: Development is the transfer of surplus labor from a low-productivity traditional sector to a capitalist modern sector; growth driven by reinvested modern-sector profits.
lac_relevance: Core dual-economy lens; LAC's traditional sector moved from rural to urban informal.

citation: Kaldor, N. Causes of the Slow Rate of Economic Growth of the United Kingdom
key_claim_paraphrased: Manufacturing is the engine of growth: increasing returns (Verdoorn) mean manufacturing output growth raises productivity in manufacturing and the whole economy.
lac_relevance: Classic case for manufacturing primacy; LAC deindustrialized early.

citation: Prebisch, R. The Economic Development of Latin America and its Principal Problems (ECLA)
key_claim_paraphrased: Center-periphery: primary exporters face declining terms of trade and absorb technology slowly; industrialization required.
lac_relevance: Foundational LAC structuralism.

citation: Baumol, W. 'Macroeconomics of Unbalanced Growth.' AER 57(3)
key_claim_paraphrased: Stagnant-productivity sectors absorb rising shares of nominal spending and employment, dragging aggregate growth.
lac_relevance: Services absorption of LAC labor implies Baumol drag.

citation: Hirschman, A.O. The Strategy of Economic Development
key_claim_paraphrased: Development proceeds through unbalanced investment in sectors with strong backward/forward linkages.
lac_relevance: Linkages from resource enclaves are a recurring LAC question.

citation: Romer, P. 'Endogenous Technological Change.' JPE 98(5)
key_claim_paraphrased: Growth driven by purposeful creation of non-rival ideas; scale of R&D effort matters.
lac_relevance: Frontier innovation is less relevant than adoption for LAC; motivates focus on diffusion.

citation: Lucas, R. 'On the Mechanics of Economic Development.' JME 22(1)
key_claim_paraphrased: Human capital accumulation with external effects can sustain growth; learning-by-doing is good-specific.
lac_relevance: Good-specific learning underpins 'some jobs better than others'.

citation: Hall, R. & Jones, C. 'Why Do Some Countries Produce So Much More Output per Worker than Others?' QJE 114(1)
key_claim_paraphrased: Most cross-country income differences reflect TFP, driven by social infrastructure (institutions and policies).
lac_relevance: Development accounting baseline for LAC TFP gap.

citation: Caselli, F. 'Accounting for Cross-Country Income Differences.' Handbook of Economic Growth
key_claim_paraphrased: Factors explain well under half of income dispersion; residual TFP dominates.
lac_relevance: Same.

citation: Acemoglu, D., Johnson, S. & Robinson, J. 'The Colonial Origins of Comparative Development.' AER 91(5)
key_claim_paraphrased: Institutions shaped by colonial settlement are a fundamental cause of income differences.
lac_relevance: Extractive institutional legacy in LAC.

citation: Engerman, S. & Sokoloff, K. 'Factor Endowments, Institutions, and Differential Paths of Growth' in How Latin America Fell Behind
key_claim_paraphrased: Endowments fostering extreme inequality produced institutions that limited broad access to schooling, land, and political voice.
lac_relevance: Deep cause of LAC divergence from North America.

citation: Hausmann, R., Pritchett, L. & Rodrik, D. 'Growth Accelerations.' JEG 10(4)
key_claim_paraphrased: Growth accelerations are frequent and mostly unpredictable; sustaining them is the hard part.
lac_relevance: LAC has accelerations (e.g. 2003-13) that did not persist.

citation: Hausmann, R. & Rodrik, D. 'Economic Development as Self-Discovery.' JDE 72(2)
key_claim_paraphrased: Discovering what a country can produce profitably is costly and imitable, so there is too little entrepreneurial experimentation.
lac_relevance: Rationale for productive development policies in LAC.

citation: Hausmann, R., Hwang, J. & Rodrik, D. 'What You Export Matters.' JEG 12(1)
key_claim_paraphrased: Countries exporting goods associated with richer countries subsequently grow faster.
lac_relevance: Export sophistication of LAC commodity exporters.

citation: Hidalgo, C. & Hausmann, R. 'The Building Blocks of Economic Complexity.' PNAS 106(26)
key_claim_paraphrased: Economic complexity (diversity and ubiquity of exports) reflects capabilities and predicts future growth.
lac_relevance: LAC complexity mostly low and stagnant (Mexico exception via assembly).

citation: Hidalgo, C., Klinger, B., Barabási, A-L. & Hausmann, R. 'The Product Space Conditions the Development of Nations.' Science 317
key_claim_paraphrased: Countries diversify into products near their current capabilities; peripheral specializations make jumps hard.
lac_relevance: Resource-based specializations sit in sparse parts of the product space.

citation: McMillan, M. & Rodrik, D. 'Globalization, Structural Change and Productivity Growth.' NBER WP 17143
key_claim_paraphrased: Since 1990 labor moved from higher- to lower-productivity sectors in Latin America and Africa (growth-reducing structural change), unlike Asia. Resource-intensive exporters fared worse; competitive exchange rates and flexible labor markets helped.
lac_relevance: Central LAC finding.

citation: Diao, X., McMillan, M. & Rodrik, D. 'The Recent Growth Boom in Developing Economies: A Structural-Change Perspective.' NBER WP 23132
key_claim_paraphrased: No recent growth acceleration outside East Asia was industrialization-led. In Latin America within-sector productivity gains drove growth while labor reallocation contributed little or negatively; in Africa the reverse. The two channels rarely operate together.
lac_relevance: Defines the LAC pattern: modern segments improve but do not absorb labor.

citation: Rodrik, D. 'Unconditional Convergence in Manufacturing.' QJE 128(1)
key_claim_paraphrased: Formal manufacturing industries show unconditional labor-productivity convergence toward the frontier, unlike whole economies.
lac_relevance: Manufacturing as escalator; LAC lost manufacturing employment share.

citation: Rodrik, D. 'Premature Deindustrialization.' JEG 21(1) (NBER WP 20935)
key_claim_paraphrased: Countries now reach peak manufacturing shares at lower income levels than early industrializers; Latin America especially hard hit; Asia and manufactures exporters insulated. Driven by globalization and labor-saving technology.
lac_relevance: Key stylized fact for LAC.

citation: Fujiwara, I. & Matsuyama, K. 'A Technology-Gap Model of Premature Deindustrialization.' AER 114(11)
key_claim_paraphrased: Baumol effect generates hump-shaped manufacturing share; countries adopting sectoral technologies with longer lags industrialize later and peak lower, with cross-country productivity dispersion largest in agriculture and smallest in manufacturing.
lac_relevance: Mechanism for LAC's early peak that does not require trade.

citation: Huneeus, F. & Rogerson, R. 'Heterogeneous Paths of Industrialization.' REStud (NBER WP 27580)
key_claim_paraphrased: Benchmark structural-change models produce hump-shaped industrial employment; differential sectoral catch-up, especially in agricultural productivity growth, explains most variation in peak industrial shares, including premature deindustrialization.
lac_relevance: Agricultural productivity growth matters for LAC's industrial peak.
notes: Fetched abstract 2026-11-02; publication year to confirm

citation: Herrendorf, B., Rogerson, R. & Valentinyi, A. 'Growth and Structural Transformation.' Handbook of Economic Growth vol. 2
key_claim_paraphrased: Survey: income and relative-price effects drive reallocation from agriculture to manufacturing to services; hump in manufacturing.
lac_relevance: Framework baseline.

citation: Duarte, M. & Restuccia, D. 'The Role of the Structural Transformation in Aggregate Productivity.' QJE 125(1)
key_claim_paraphrased: Cross-country productivity gaps are largest and most persistent in services; low services productivity drags aggregate catch-up as services shares grow.
lac_relevance: Services productivity is the binding gap for LAC.

citation: Gollin, D., Lagakos, D. & Waugh, M. 'The Agricultural Productivity Gap.' QJE 129(2)
key_claim_paraphrased: Value added per worker is much higher outside agriculture, especially in poor countries; the gap shrinks but remains large after adjusting for hours and human capital.
lac_relevance: Supports dual-economy gaps as real; measurement caution.

citation: Porzio, T., Rossi, F. & Santangelo, G. 'The Human Side of Structural Transformation.' AER 112(8)
key_claim_paraphrased: About half the global decline in agricultural employment comes from new cohorts; human capital accounts for roughly 40% of the decline at fixed prices, about half that in general equilibrium.
lac_relevance: Schooling expansion in LAC fed reallocation; but into which jobs?

citation: Hsieh, C-T. & Klenow, P. 'Misallocation and Manufacturing TFP in China and India.' QJE 124(4)
key_claim_paraphrased: Dispersion of marginal products across plants implies large TFP gains from reallocation.
lac_relevance: Method used for LAC estimates.

citation: Hsieh, C-T. & Klenow, P. 'The Life Cycle of Plants in India and Mexico.' QJE 129(3)
key_claim_paraphrased: Surviving plants in Mexico and India grow far less with age than US plants; flat life cycles imply large TFP losses.
lac_relevance: Mexico case.

citation: Restuccia, D. & Rogerson, R. 'Policy Distortions and Aggregate Productivity with Heterogeneous Establishments.' RED 11(4)
key_claim_paraphrased: Idiosyncratic distortions that tax productive and subsidize unproductive plants can cut TFP substantially.
lac_relevance: Mechanism behind Levy's argument.

citation: Busso, M., Madrigal, L. & Pagés, C. 'Productivity and Resource Misallocation in Latin America.' IDB WP / BE J. Macro 13(1)
key_claim_paraphrased: Latin American TFP has not risen since the mid-1970s; with firm data from 10 countries, productivity dispersion and misallocation are much larger than in the US; efficient allocation would raise manufacturing TFP by roughly 45-127%.
lac_relevance: Key LAC magnitude.

citation: Pagés, C. (ed.) The Age of Productivity: Transforming Economies from the Bottom Up. IDB DIA
key_claim_paraphrased: LAC's income gap is mainly a productivity gap, with low productivity concentrated in services and small firms; diagnose sector by sector.
lac_relevance: Foundational IDB diagnosis.

citation: Levy, S. Under-Rewarded Efforts: The Elusive Quest for Prosperity in Mexico. IDB
key_claim_paraphrased: Mexico's per capita growth averaged ~1.2% (1996-2015) despite reforms. Misallocation driven by tax, social insurance and labor rules that tax productive formal firms and subsidize informal ones; informal firms are >90% of firms, ~55% of employment and ~50% less productive; education and infrastructure not the main cause.
lac_relevance: Institutions-to-misallocation mechanism for LAC.

citation: Eslava, M., Haltiwanger, J. & Pinzón, A. 'Job Creation in Colombia vs the U.S.: Up or Out Dynamics Meets the Life Cycle of Plants.' NBER WP 25550
key_claim_paraphrased: Colombian plants grow less with age than US plants, mainly because of a thinner upper tail of high-growth young plants and weaker selection; ~87% of establishments are micro (~32% of employment); only ~8% of small-born plants become medium/large.
lac_relevance: Firm dynamics in LAC.

citation: La Porta, R. & Shleifer, A. 'Informality and Development.' JEP 28(3)
key_claim_paraphrased: Informal firms are small, unproductive, run by low-education managers, and rarely become formal; growth comes from formal-firm expansion replacing them.
lac_relevance: Dual view of informality.

citation: Ulyssea, G. 'Firms, Informality, and Development: Theory and Evidence from Brazil.' AER 108(8)
key_claim_paraphrased: Informality combines 'parasite', 'survival' and 'exclusion' firms; reducing entry costs into formality has different effects from tighter enforcement; enforcement can raise TFP but lower employment/welfare.
lac_relevance: Heterogeneous informality; trade-offs.

citation: Hsieh, C-T. & Olken, B. 'The Missing "Missing Middle".' JEP 28(3)
key_claim_paraphrased: Developing countries have many tiny firms and few large ones, but no evident 'missing middle' bump; thresholds matter less than claimed.
lac_relevance: Caution on size-threshold stories.

citation: Cole, H., Ohanian, L., Riascos, A. & Schmitz, J. 'Latin America in the Rearview Mirror.' JME 52(1)
key_claim_paraphrased: Latin America is the only poor Western group not closing the gap with the US; the gap is TFP not human capital, plausibly due to international and domestic competitive barriers; cutting barriers raised productivity in documented cases.
lac_relevance: Competition-barriers diagnosis.

citation: Restuccia, D. 'The Latin American Development Problem: An Interpretation.' Economía 13(2):69-100
key_claim_paraphrased: LAC's relative income decline since the mid-20th century is a productivity problem; policies and institutions that misallocate resources across producers are the leading interpretation.
lac_relevance: Synthesis of misallocation view for LAC.
notes: Bibliographic data verified; content from memory, full text not reachable

citation: World Bank. Competition: The Missing Ingredient for Growth? LAC Economic Review, April 2024
key_claim_paraphrased: LAC growth forecasts lowest of all regions; markups high, markets concentrated with a few large firms and many tiny ones; about 70% of workers self-employed or in firms <10 workers.
lac_relevance: Competition + firm-structure diagnosis.
notes: Fetched news summary of report 2026-11-02; read the report itself later

citation: IMF. Regional Economic Outlook: Western Hemisphere, October 2025 (and Khachatryan presentation, IMF-OECD conference 2025)
key_claim_paraphrased: LA5 TFP ~0.52 of US (2019); LA5 TFP growth about -0.7%/yr 2000-19 vs positive in Emerging Europe/Asia; misallocation costs ~16% of TFP vs AEs; weakness concentrated in within-firm productivity of survivors; reallocation contributes ~0; giving LA5 other regions' industry mix barely changes TFP growth. Frictions: size-based policies, finance, competition.
lac_relevance: Key recent evidence: within-firm not between-sector.
notes: Fetched slides 2026-11-02; check the REO chapter text later

citation: ECLAC. Press release on growth projections, 2025 (Economic Survey / Preliminary Overview)
key_claim_paraphrased: Region in a prolonged period of low growth: ~2.2% (2025) and ~2.3% (2026); weak domestic demand; ECLAC frames 'traps' of low growth and high inequality.
lac_relevance: Current context.

citation: World Bank. World Development Report 2024: The Middle-Income Trap
key_claim_paraphrased: Middle-income countries must move from investment (1i) to investment+infusion of foreign technology (2i) to adding innovation (3i); only 34 middle-income countries reached high income since 1990; incumbents and entrenched institutions are obstacles.
lac_relevance: Most LAC countries are upper-middle income stuck at '2i'.

citation: Kremer, M., Willis, J. & You, Y. 'Converging to Convergence.' NBER Macro Annual 36 (WP 29484)
key_claim_paraphrased: Unconditional convergence has emerged since ~1990/2000; policies, institutions and human capital also converged; non-Solow correlates lost predictive power.
lac_relevance: LAC is an exception to the recent convergence trend - needs explanation.

citation: Comin, D. & Mestieri, M. 'If Technology Has Arrived Everywhere, Why Has Income Diverged?' AEJ: Macro 10(3)
key_claim_paraphrased: Adoption lags have converged across countries but penetration (intensity of use) has diverged; ~80% of the income divergence since 1820 attributed to these diffusion patterns.
lac_relevance: Intensive-margin adoption = LAC within-firm problem.

citation: Cirera, X. & Maloney, W. The Innovation Paradox. World Bank
key_claim_paraphrased: Developing countries under-invest in innovation despite high potential returns because complementary capabilities (managerial, human capital, state capacity) are missing; build management first; 'capabilities escalator'.
lac_relevance: Maloney is LAC-focused; management gap.

citation: Bloom, N. & Van Reenen, J. 'Measuring and Explaining Management Practices Across Firms and Countries.' QJE 122(4)
key_claim_paraphrased: Management practices vary widely and explain productivity differences; weak competition and family-primogeniture firms have worse management.
lac_relevance: Management in LAC firms (Brazil/Mexico/Argentina low scores).

citation: Lagakos, D., Moll, B., Porzio, T., Qian, N. & Schoellman, T. 'Life Cycle Wage Growth across Countries.' JPE 126(2)
key_claim_paraphrased: Experience-wage profiles are on average about twice as steep in rich as in poor countries; education explains about a third; consistent with less on-the-job human capital accumulation or more search frictions in poor countries.
lac_relevance: Jobs differ in learning content; central to 'good jobs' framework.

citation: Rodrik, D. & Sandhu, R. 'Servicing Development: Productive Upgrading of Labor-Absorbing Services in Developing Economies.' NBER WP 32738; Global Policy 16(2)
key_claim_paraphrased: Manufacturing creates few jobs in developing economies; urban employment is informal, low-productivity services; upgrading labor-absorbing services is necessary. Four strategies: expand large productive firms, public inputs for small firms, technologies complementing low-skill labor, vocational training with wrap-around support.
lac_relevance: Directly relevant to LAC urban informality.

citation: Rodrik, D. & Sabel, C. 'Building a Good Jobs Economy.' (HKS WP; VoxDev)
key_claim_paraphrased: The scarcity of good jobs generates social externalities (exclusion, inequality, political backlash); remedy combines productivist policies, competition and collaborative, iterative public-private governance.
lac_relevance: Normative frame for 'good jobs'.

citation: Diao, X., Ellis, M., McMillan, M. & Rodrik, D. 'Africa's Manufacturing Puzzle: Evidence from Tanzanian and Ethiopian Firms.' NBER WP 28344
key_claim_paraphrased: Within manufacturing, larger firms raise productivity but add few jobs while small firms absorb labor with no productivity growth; linked to capital-intensive global technologies.
lac_relevance: Template for 'segment dualism' within sectors; check whether it holds in LAC.

citation: Juhász, R., Lane, N. & Rodrik, D. 'The New Economics of Industrial Policy.' Annual Review of Economics (NBER WP 31538)
key_claim_paraphrased: New causal evidence is more favorable to industrial policy than the older correlational literature; effects are context-dependent; tools beyond subsidies; governance central.
lac_relevance: Policy implications for LAC productive development.

citation: Atkin, D., Costinot, A. & Fukui, M. 'Globalization and the Ladder of Development: Pushed to the Top or Held at the Bottom?' NBER WP 29500
key_claim_paraphrased: Capability growth rises with the average complexity of a country's industry mix (causal evidence via WTO accessions); dynamic losses from trade small for the median country but large for some.
lac_relevance: Formal evidence that what you produce affects capability growth.

citation: ILO & World Bank. 'Buffer or Bottleneck? Employment Exposure to Generative AI and the Digital Divide in Latin America.' ILO WP 121
key_claim_paraphrased: 26-38% of LAC jobs exposed to GenAI; 8-14% could gain via augmentation; 2-5% face full automation; up to half of augmentation gains (~17m jobs) blocked by digital divide; benefits skew to formal, urban, educated workers.
lac_relevance: New-technology channel for LAC good jobs.

citation: Rodrik, D. 'Prospects for Global Economic Convergence Under New Technologies.' (Brookings / HKS)
key_claim_paraphrased: New technologies are skill- and capital-biased and favor tradable activities with limited labor absorption, weakening the manufacturing escalator.
lac_relevance: Background to 'unbundling' idea.

citation: Nayyar, G., Hallward-Driemeier, M. & Davies, E. At Your Service? The Promise of Services-Led Development. World Bank
key_claim_paraphrased: Some services (ICT, professional, finance, transport) share manufacturing's growth features (scale, innovation, spillovers) but are skill-intensive; others absorb labor with limited productivity growth.
lac_relevance: Services heterogeneity; LAC services-led paths.

citation: Lederman, D. & Maloney, W. (eds.) Natural Resources: Neither Curse nor Destiny. World Bank/Stanford
key_claim_paraphrased: Resource abundance is not inherently harmful; outcomes depend on institutions, knowledge capabilities and diversification of the resource-based economy.
lac_relevance: Resource-based development path for LAC.

citation: Sachs, J. & Warner, A. 'Natural Resource Abundance and Economic Growth.' NBER WP 5398
key_claim_paraphrased: Resource-abundant economies grew more slowly (Dutch disease, rent seeking).
lac_relevance: Contested; LAC is a main test.

citation: Ramey, G. & Ramey, V. 'Cross-Country Evidence on the Link Between Volatility and Growth.' AER 85(5)
key_claim_paraphrased: Higher volatility is associated with lower growth.
lac_relevance: LAC macro volatility (commodity cycles, sudden stops).

citation: Rodrik, D. 'The Real Exchange Rate and Economic Growth.' Brookings Papers 2008(2)
key_claim_paraphrased: Undervaluation fosters growth in developing countries by expanding tradables, which suffer more from institutional and market failures.
lac_relevance: Commodity-driven RER appreciation in LAC.

citation: Ocampo, J.A. 'The Quest for Dynamic Efficiency: Structural Dynamics and Economic Growth in Developing Countries' in Beyond Reforms
key_claim_paraphrased: Growth depends on the economy's capacity to generate new dynamic activities and to link them domestically; neo-structuralist synthesis.
lac_relevance: Neo-structuralist LAC view.

citation: Fajnzylber, F. Industrialización en América Latina: de la 'caja negra' al 'casillero vacío' (CEPAL)
key_claim_paraphrased: Almost no LAC country achieved both dynamic growth and equity ('empty box'); requires endogenous technical progress.
lac_relevance: Growth-equity link specific to LAC.

citation: Kehoe, T. & Ruhl, K. 'Why Have Economic Reforms in Mexico Not Generated Growth?' JEL 48(4)
key_claim_paraphrased: Mexico's reforms did not yield growth; candidate explanations include financial frictions, contract enforcement and labor-market rigidities rather than trade policy.
lac_relevance: Reform-without-growth puzzle.

citation: Maloney, W. 'Informality Revisited.' World Development 32(7)
key_claim_paraphrased: Much informal work is voluntary and reflects preferences and low formal-sector productivity, not only exclusion.
lac_relevance: Counterpoint to dual view.

citation: Acemoglu, D., Aghion, P. & Zilibotti, F. 'Distance to Frontier, Selection, and Economic Growth.' JEEA 4(1)
key_claim_paraphrased: Investment/imitation-based strategies suit countries far from the frontier; near the frontier, selection and innovation become key, and failing to switch causes traps.
lac_relevance: Theory behind middle-income trap and LAC import-substitution exhaustion.

citation: Buera, F. & Kaboski, J. 'The Rise of the Service Economy.' AER 102(6)
key_claim_paraphrased: The rise of services reflects growth in skill-intensive services as income rises (demand for high-skill services and marketization).
lac_relevance: Skill-intensive services as a growth driver.

citation: Felipe, J., Mehta, A. & Rhee, C. 'Manufacturing Matters... but It's the Jobs that Count.' Cambridge J. Econ 43(1)
key_claim_paraphrased: Countries became rich after achieving high manufacturing employment shares (around 18%+); manufacturing output share is a weaker predictor.
lac_relevance: Employment, not output, in manufacturing matters.

citation: Hsieh, C-T. & Klenow, P. 'Development Accounting.' AEJ: Macro 2(1)
key_claim_paraphrased: TFP accounts for most income differences; human capital quality and indirect effects of TFP on capital also matter.
lac_relevance: Baseline.

citation: Daude, C. & Fernández-Arias, E. 'On the Role of Productivity and Factor Accumulation in Economic Development in Latin America and the Caribbean.' IDB WP
key_claim_paraphrased: LAC's income gap and lack of convergence are explained mainly by low and stagnant TFP rather than factor accumulation.
lac_relevance: LAC development accounting.

citation: Eichengreen, B., Park, D. & Shin, K. 'When Fast-Growing Economies Slow Down.' Asian Econ Papers 11(1)
key_claim_paraphrased: Fast growers tend to slow sharply around $15-17k (PPP) per capita; slowdowns associated with TFP decline.
lac_relevance: Middle-income slowdown context.

citation: Bloom, N., Mahajan, A., McKenzie, D. & Roberts, J. 'Why Do Firms in Developing Countries Have Low Productivity?' AER P&P 100(2)
key_claim_paraphrased: Low productivity in developing-country firms reflects poor management, limited competition, weak delegation (trust/contract enforcement) and constrained growth of good firms.
lac_relevance: Mechanisms for within-firm stagnation.
